subject: Model-match qualification & next steps for MedBridge eval
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@medbridge.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 18:05:00 +0000
Subject: Model-match qualification & next steps for MedBridge eval

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the call earlier — we covered a lot. Quick recap from my side and a request for the concrete next steps so we can scope this internally:

- Goal: run a blind, customer-specific eval to compare candidate models on our clinical-note summarization and discharge-summary QA tasks. We need objective scoring and a plan to detect regressions after rollout.
- Data sensitivity: notes will contain PHI; we'll need guidance on de-identification or an on-prem / VPC flow.
- Desired deliverable: a ranked model recommendation + per-task metrics and example failure modes.

Can you send: recommended model candidates (small/med/large), the dataset/schema format you need, a short scoring rubric, and an estimated timeline & cost for a 2k-item blind run? Procurement will also want a rough SOW line item to review.

I'll loop in procurement (procurement@medbridge.com) after I have the ballpark. We can share a de-id subset (500 notes) if that helps accelerate.

Thanks,
Sanjay Rao
Head of Applied ML
MedBridge Health

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@medbridge.com>
Cc: procurement@medbridge.com
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 20:10:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Model-match qualification & next steps for MedBridge eval

Sanjay — great talking earlier. Appreciate the clear goals. Below is a concise plan and the artifacts we typically ask for to run an initial customer-specific eval on Redwood. I attached a skeleton schema and a small prompts example to make it concrete.

Recommended model candidates (to include in the blind run):
- redwood-rlhf-13b (low-latency, good baseline for summarization)
- llm-open-70b (high-quality reference; expect higher cost/latency)
- redwood-quant-8b (quantized variant for cost-constrained deployments)

Why these? We generally include a cost-optimized quantized candidate, a mid/high-quality baseline, and the lightweight real-time candidate so you can trade off quality vs latency. We can add any third-party model you prefer.

Dataset & format (what we need):
- Preferred: JSONL, UTF-8, newline-delimited. Each record: {"id": string, "input": string, "reference": string, "task": string, "metadata": {"site_id": string, "redaction_level": string}}
- Minimum size for meaningful metrics: 500 examples/task (we can run smaller pilots). Aim for 2k total if you want statistically stable comparisons.
- I attached medbridge_eval_schema.csv (column layout) and sample_prompts.jsonl.

Scoring & rubric (short version):
- Automated: ROUGE-L / BERTScore for summarization; exact-match / F1 for QA (span-based).
- Human spot-check: 200 examples sampled, 3-judge majority vote, categories: accurate/partial/missing/hallucination.
- Acceptance thresholds: we typically ask for +5 pts ROUGE-L over current baseline or <5% hallucination for green-light; we can tune thresholds to your risk profile.

Security / hosting options:
- Hosted: fastest turnaround (we keep data in our isolated buckets with AES-256 at rest).
- Private (VPC or on-prem): available for PHI if you require the data to stay in your cloud. We'll need a short runbook and network setup.

Timeline & costs (ballpark):
- Pilot (500 de-identified examples): 3-5 business days to run + QA, cost estimate $800–$1,500 depending on model mix.
- Full 2k blind run: 5–8 business days, $2,500–$6,000 depending on the number of models and whether human scoring is included.

Next steps (proposed):
1) You confirm desired hosting option (Hosted vs Private).
2) You share a de-id 500-example JSONL (or give S3/Drive access).
3) We run the pilot, share raw metrics + failure examples, then align on a 2k run if results look promising.

Attachments: medbridge_eval_schema.csv (column definitions), sample_prompts.jsonl (example records), redwood_quickstart.pdf (quickstart checklist).

Drive examples & eval format: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-eval-examples
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/MDG-2026-1142

If you'd like, Rishi (cc'd) can provide a short scoring template and a regression-monitoring plan.

Best,

Evelyn Hart
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
E: evelyn@redwood.ai

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@medbridge.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 09:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Model-match qualification & next steps for MedBridge eval

Sanjay — looping in a couple of concrete scoring and operational details to avoid back-and-forth later.

Quick scoring template (we'll produce this as a CSV you can review):
- model_id, task, example_id, auto_metric_score (ROUGE-L / F1), human_label (accurate/partial/missing/hallucination), human_confidence (1-3), notes
- Aggregates: median ROUGE-L (with 95% CI), percent_hallucination, percent_partial.

Suggested thresholds and checks:
- Summarization: median ROUGE-L delta > +3 points vs your current baseline to consider a candidate "better"; flag any model with >7% hallucination rate for further review.
- QA: span-F1 > 0.7 and <3% false-positive hallucination.

Regression and monitoring:
- Use Redwood Optimize to pin the production variant and run daily sampling evals on a rolling 7-day window. We can wire alerts to Slack for regressions beyond your tolerance.

Operational notes for PHI: if you prefer Private/VPC, we'll provide a CloudFormation/Terraform snippet to provision a customer-managed bucket and a service endpoint that keeps data inside your account; presigned S3 upload is also an option for quick pilots.

Estimated resource/time: for a blind 2k-run across 3 models + 200 human spot-checks we typically allocate one engineer half-time for 1 week (for run and initial triage) + 2 QA raters for 3 days. Cost math included in Evelyn's ballpark.

If you can share a de-id 500 sample this week, we can kick off a pilot and have a results deck by next Wednesday.

—Rishi
Head of Applied ML Ops | Redwood Inference

2) Ballpark cost for 2k examples across three models (no human scoring) — can you confirm the lower estimate ($2.5k) holds if we run quant + rlhf + open-70b?
3) If we go Private (VPC) what's the rough lead time for networking + access?

Procurement is cc'd and will flag NDA / SOW questions. We'll aim to send the 500 notes by Friday if we get the upload details.

Sanjay
Head of Applied ML
